summary.text: An electric generator is a device that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy for an outside circuit.
Steam, gas and water turbines, engines, wind turbines or even a hand crank can spin it.
It works on Faraday's law, and generators supply nearly all the electricity on the world's power grids.

facts.label: Opposite device
facts.value: An electric motor turns electrical energy into motion

facts.label: Dynamo output
facts.value: Pulsing direct current through a commutator

facts.label: Voltage and turns
facts.value: Output voltage is proportional to the number of turns

items.prompt: A wind turbine's spinning blades are connected to a generator. What does the generator do with the motion?

options.label: Turns it into electrical energy for a circuit
Turns it into heat to warm the blades
Stores it as chemical fuel
Turns it into more wind

items.explain: A generator converts mechanical energy from a source such as a wind turbine to electrical energy.

items.prompt: Why did early inventors wind wire into coils rather than using a single copper disc?

options.label: Coils simply look much neater
Coils are always cheaper than discs
A copper disc cannot spin at all
More turns give a higher voltage

items.explain: The disc gave very low voltage through a single path; multiple turns produced higher voltage, proportional to the number of turns.

items.prompt: Why was Faraday's disk generator inefficient?

options.label: Current ran backwards outside the magnet, wasting power
The disc was too light to spin at speed
The magnet was made of weak wood
It produced only alternating current

items.explain: Counterflows of current in regions outside the magnetic field limited output and heated the copper.

items.prompt: A coil spins in a magnetic field with no commutator. What kind of current comes out?

options.label: Perfectly steady direct current
Alternating current, reversing each half turn
No current at all in the coil
A single pulse and then nothing

items.explain: A coil rotating in a magnetic field gives a current that changes direction with each 180 degree rotation.

items.prompt: A farmer cranks a spare electric motor backwards by hand and a lamp lights. What is happening?

options.label: The motor is working as a generator
The lamp is somehow making the motor spin
Motors cannot work in this way at all
The lamp runs on static charge from the hand

items.explain: Motors and generators are very similar, and some motors generate power if their shaft is rotated.

items.prompt: Why were electrostatic generators never used to power cities?

options.label: They burned far too much fuel each day
They gave high voltage but only low current
They needed far too much cooling water
They only worked during the night

items.explain: They made very high voltage but low current, and were inefficient and hard to insulate, so power ratings stayed low.
